answer: Each agent can post a bond that is locked in a shared escrow, while a vertex’s influence grows only after other bonded agents independently endorse its work and those endorsements survive a challenge period. A garden of agents controlled by one attacker cannot cheaply manufacture this trust: every fake identity needs capital at risk, and colluding endorsements expose the whole cluster to slashing. The bond acts as an anchor, making mass identity creation costly rather than merely a matter of generating new keys.
